reason: This passage (Genesis 22:1-19, the Binding of Isaac) depicts biblical patriarchs and their families, not 'regular people' in the conventional sense. The primary human figure is Abraham, a founding patriarch and man of God, portrayed as exemplary in his faith and obedience. While Abraham and Isaac are indeed portrayed very favorably—Abraham as faithful and wise, Isaac as trusting and obedient—they are exceptional religious figures chosen by God, not ordinary people. The young servants mentioned briefly are not characterized in ways that would allow assessment of their portrayal. The passage focuses on a divine test of an extraordinary biblical figure, not on the depiction of regular, non-exceptional people.
